title: Things to Do in Thekkady: Periyar Boat Safari, Jungle Walks & Spice Gardens
seoTitle: Things to Do in Thekkady: Periyar, Spices & Treks | Kudozz Club
description: Things to do in Thekkady: the Periyar lake boat safari, bamboo rafting and nature walks run by the forest department, spice plantation tours, Kathakali and kalaripayattu in Kumily, Chellarkovil and Ramakkalmedu viewpoints, Gavi, and the Mangala Devi temple festival.
dek: The gateway to Periyar Tiger Reserve in Kerala's cardamom hills, where elephants come down to a forest lake and spice gardens surround the town.
searchIntent: Families and couples spending one or two days in Thekkady between Munnar and the backwaters.

hero.alt: Periyar lake in Periyar Tiger Reserve, Thekkady

intro: Thekkady, in Idukki district near the Tamil Nadu border, is the base for visiting Periyar Tiger Reserve, one of India's best-known protected areas. The lake at its heart was formed in 1895 by the Mullaperiyar Dam, and the drowned trees still stand in the water. The neighbouring town of Kumily is where most hotels, spice shops and restaurants are.

The things to do in Thekkady centre on Periyar: a boat safari on the lake, and eco-tourism activities such as nature walks, bamboo rafting and border hikes led by trained local guides, many of them from forest-dependent communities. Outside the park are spice plantations, cultural shows, viewpoints over Tamil Nadu and the forest eco-tourism at Gavi.
One to two days is enough. October to April is the best time; sightings are often better in the drier months.

Go on a guided nature walk

items.name: Take a boat safari on the lake
body: Boats run by the forest department and KTDC cruise Periyar lake for about 90 minutes, past drowned trees and forested banks where elephants, gaur, sambar, wild boar and otters come to the water. The first boat of the morning usually has the best chances. Tickets are sold online and at the counter, and queues can be long in season.

items.name: Go on a guided nature walk
body: Short nature walks of two to three hours, led by trained guides, go into the forest in small groups. You may see birds, giant squirrels, Nilgiri langurs and signs of larger animals. Leech socks are provided in the wet season.

items.name: Try bamboo rafting
body: The full-day bamboo rafting programme combines forest trekking with a slow raft ride on the lake, in small groups with armed guards and guides. It is one of the best ways to experience Periyar and needs booking in advance.

items.name: Hike the border trail
body: The border hiking programme follows the ridge along the Kerala–Tamil Nadu border inside the reserve, with views over the plains. Other options include night patrols and the multi-day Tiger Trail. Programmes change; check with the eco-tourism centre.

items.name: Tour a spice plantation
body: Spice gardens around Kumily offer guided walks showing cardamom, pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg, cloves, vanilla and coffee. Many sell spices at the end of the tour.

items.name: Watch Kathakali and kalaripayattu
body: Kumily has several small theatres with evening shows of Kathakali, often with the make-up session open to watch, and kalaripayattu, Kerala's martial art.

items.name: Shop for spices and tea
body: Kumily's main road is lined with spice shops. Cardamom, pepper, cloves and tea are good buys. Vandanmedu, nearby, has cardamom auction centres.

items.name: See the view from Chellarkovil
body: Chellarkovil, about 15 km away, looks down steep slopes into the plains of Tamil Nadu, with a small waterfall in the monsoon.

items.name: Visit Ramakkalmedu
body: Ramakkalmedu, about 40 km away, is a windy hilltop with wind turbines, rock formations and a large statue of a Kuravan and Kurathi, figures from local legend. The view over Tamil Nadu is wide.

items.name: Take a jeep trip to Gavi
body: Gavi, in the forests south of Thekkady, is reached through a controlled forest route and is run as an eco-tourism destination by the Kerala Forest Development Corporation, with trekking, boating and stays. Entry is regulated; book in advance.

items.name: See the Mangala Devi temple festival
body: Mangala Devi Kannagi Temple, on a hilltop inside the reserve, is open to pilgrims only on Chitra Pournami, the full moon in April or May, when thousands walk or drive up.

items.name: Winter (October to February)
body: Cool, pleasant weather and good conditions for walks and rafting. It is the busiest season, so book boat tickets and eco-tourism programmes early.

items.name: Summer (March to May)
body: The forest dries out and animals come to the lake to drink, which often improves sightings on the boat safari. Afternoons are warm but the hills stay cooler than the plains.

items.name: Monsoon (June to September)
body: Heavy rain, leeches and lush forest. Some programmes are suspended or shortened in heavy weather.

oneDay: Take the first boat safari on Periyar lake, then a short nature walk. After lunch, tour a spice plantation and drive to Chellarkovil for the view, ending with a Kathakali show in Kumily.
tips: Kochi airport is about four hours away; Kottayam is the nearest major railway station.
Book boat safaris and eco-tourism programmes online in advance in peak season.
Wear neutral colours on walks and follow your guide's instructions.
Carry leech socks and rain gear in the monsoon.

faqs.q: What are the best things to do in Thekkady?
faqs.a: Take a boat safari on Periyar lake, go on a nature walk or bamboo rafting, tour a spice plantation, watch Kathakali, see Chellarkovil and Ramakkalmedu, and visit Gavi.

faqs.q: Can you see tigers in Periyar?
faqs.a: Tigers are present but rarely seen. Elephants, gaur, sambar and birds are much more common.

faqs.q: How many days are enough for Thekkady?
What is the best time to visit Thekkady?
How do I book the Periyar boat safari?
faqs.a: Tickets are sold online through the official Periyar Tiger Reserve and KTDC booking systems, and at the counter near the boat landing. Book ahead in peak season, especially for the first boat.
